summary: Lewis County lookout planned in 1926 and staffed in 1927-28 per newspaper transcriptions; the listing marks it removed, with no date given.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed with no date given; no source describes what, if anything, is left on the peak today.

events.note: J. J. Modine named as the lookout at Twin Sisters among the federal fire wardens in Lewis County
April 1926 newspaper item: a tower was to be built on the Twin Sisters peak above the Cowlitz Valley; completion not stated in the sources read
July 1927 newspaper item: Albert Westall and his wife were to stay two months at the Twin Sisters station
By September 1928 the Westalls had come down after a couple of months at the station in the employ of the Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both secondhand. The 1922-1928 items are transcriptions of Chehalis Bee-Nugget clippings on a hobbyist site, without page numbers. The Mossyrock history mentions Twin Sisters only as a landmark in photo captions, not as a lookout. The firelookout.org county index has no Lewis County Twin Sisters entry. Search results mixed in other Twin Sisters towers: the Colorado lookout in Rocky Mountain National Park (built 1914, removed 1977) and a Ferry County tower (FFLOS US 1475, WA 375, gone by 1975). Do not merge those records. The 1922 item says Rainier National Forest; the listing gives Gifford Pinchot National Forest. The Removed tag has no date. Suggested checks: the Chehalis Bee-Nugget originals (Washington Digital Newspapers) and Gifford Pinchot National Forest heritage records for a build year and a removal year. Page reads went over the brief's budget of six.
